canopy.silhouette: tall rounded crown on straight grey bole

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two oblong green cotyledons, then pinnate leaves of 3-7 broad, rounded leaflets (the first may carry only one to three). The sapling is a slender whip with a narrow crown, tolerating some side shade, readily browsed by cattle and goats and able to resprout; later it builds a tall, dense, dark-green domed crown.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Database Dalbergia latifolia (20-40 m; harvested at 30-40 yr; flowers Dec-Mar; white flowers 0.5-1 cm in axillary panicles; brown oblong-lanceolate pods with 1-4 seeds; germination 7-25 d, 45-80%); Wikipedia (slow-growing monsoon-forest tree). Height curve, fruiting age and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Database (flowering Dec-Mar; white papilionaceous flowers 0.5-1 cm in axillary panicles; brown oblong-lanceolate pods pointed at both ends, 1-4 seeds). Pod length, ripening, persistence (as in D. sissoo, pods hang on for months), set and crop estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with distinctive three-lobed cotyledons, then a few simple or three-parted toothed leaves before pinnate ones. The sapling is a slender, fast-growing whip with glossy pinnate leaves bunched at the tip, its bark already smooth, copper-red and peeling in thin papery flakes over green. Stuck-in branches root and grow into trees (living fences).
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 30 m, fast growth from cuttings, shiny dark red peeling bark; fruit a 3-valved capsule with a red fatty aril 5-6 mm, main fruiting Mar-Apr, bird-dispersed); germination, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (small 3-valved top-shaped fruits enclosing one seed with a red lipid-rich aril; ripe mainly Mar-Apr in the north of the range, some all year; birds such as orioles and vireos take the arils); small greenish flowers before the leaves; timings and counts estimated.

canopy.silhouette: crooked bare tree ablaze with orange flowers

growth.juvenile_note: Big flat seeds sprout in 1-3 weeks. The seedling grows a thick, carrot-like taproot and a shoot of large trifoliate leaves with broad, leathery, rounded leaflets; in drought or frost the shoot may die back for a few years before a crooked, rough-barked stem gets away.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 15 m, slow-growing, dry-season deciduous, flowers Feb-Apr, not every year); Troup, Silviculture of Indian Trees (seedling die-back and strong taproot, light demander); germination, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (bright orange-red parrot-beak flowers 2.5 cm long in racemes to 15 cm on leafless branches, Feb-Apr; flat pod 15-20 x 4-5 cm with one seed near the tip); nectar-feeding birds (sunbirds, mynas, bulbuls) and squirrels as pollinators; pods ripen May-Jun; counts estimated.

canopy.name: Grandidier's baobab

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings have simple first leaves before digitate leaves with many leaflets. Young trees are straight, slender, fast whips (about 2 m in 2 years) with smooth grey-green bark and thin horizontal branches. The massive, smooth, reddish-grey cylindrical trunk with a flat-topped crown of branches develops only after decades.
growth.source: Useful Tropical Plants (2 m tall within 2 yr from seed; 12-15 m and 60 cm bole at 12 yr in cultivation); worldplants.ca (germination 2-6 weeks); simple juvenile leaves as in other baobabs; first flowering and age estimated from A. digitata and Patrut radiocarbon work on Malagasy baobabs

canopy.source: SW Madagascar dry forest; the Avenue. Tall smooth cylinders with a flat crown. All 8 Kew-accepted species. Deciduous in the dry season, bat-pollinated white flowers at night, fruit by mammals.

growth.juvenile_note: Almost never grows from seed: it flowers rarely and sets virtually no seed, so new clumps start from culm or branch pieces (often river-borne) that root and sprout within weeks. A young clump is a few thin leafy shoots; each rainy season it sends up thicker culms until, after 3-7 years, full-size green or golden-striped culms 10-20 m tall shoot up in a couple of months.
growth.source: Wikipedia (culms 10-20 m, 4-10 cm thick; flowering uncommon, whole populations bloom at intervals of several decades, no seed due to irregular meiosis; spread by culm and branch cuttings; clump usually survives); culm lifespan and times estimated. germination_days = cutting to shoot.

shrub.silhouette: felted grey leaves on a short thick stem

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds are dust-fine; seedlings (and plantlets from fallen leaves) form a small rosette of thick, triangular, wavy-edged leaves densely felted with brown-to-silver velvet hairs. The single stem then lengthens, shedding lower leaves and leaving knobbly scars, so the young plant looks like a felted rosette on a stick before it branches into a gaunt, tree-like succulent.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Kalanchoe beharensis: 1-2 m+ succulent shrub, felted triangular leaves in decussate pairs, small yellowish urn-shaped flowers ~7 mm in 50-60 cm branched corymbs, spring-summer; roots readily from leaf and stem cuttings); growth rate and ages estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (urn-shaped yellowish flowers ~7 mm in a tall branched corymb); Kalanchoe fruits are small dry follicles shedding dust seeds; plants contain toxic bufadienolides. Season in Madagascar, pollinators, timings and counts estimated.

The seedling runs straight out over the sand as a cord-like runner that roots at the nodes and branches, spreading many metres into a net of runners and leathery leaves across the upper beach and foredune.

Plant lifespan estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are small rosettes of narrow leaves already edged with hooked spines. They grow into big, fierce rosettes of long arching leaves with curved spines; at flowering the centre turns bright red. Each rosette flowers once and dies, but stolons build dense, impenetrable colonies.

ground.silhouette: tussock with tangled twisted black awns

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings appear with the first big rains, often from seeds that drilled themselves into the soil with their hygroscopic twisting awns: a flat, bluish-green tuft of folded leaves that tillers into a loose tussock during its first wet season. Mature culms carry dark spikes whose long brown awns twist and tangle together into the typical 'tanglehead'.
growth.source: Tropical Forages factsheet (Heteropogon contortus: seed dormancy up to ~12 months, germination optimum 30-35 C, fertile tillers 0.5-1.5 m, tolerates light shade, flowers from late January in the south); NSW DPIRD GrassedUp (relatively short-lived perennial, growth starts with first rains); timings estimated.

The rosette becomes a stiff, spreading fan of long, narrow-triangular grey-green leaves; it flowers once with flattened, paddle-like spikes of overlapping red, yellow or green bracts and violet tubular flowers, then pups and dies.

Seed-to-flower time and rosette age estimated from bromeliad horticulture.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are minute grey tufts of thread-like leaves on bark, but most new plants start as windblown or bird-carried fragments. A young plant is a short, curly chain of silvery-grey scaly stems with 2-6 cm thread leaves, lengthening over years into festoons that hang 1-6 m (rarely 8 m) from branches, with tiny three-petalled flowers in spring.
growth.source: Wikipedia Spanish moss (leaves 2-6 cm x 1 mm; hanging festoons to 6 m, rarely 8 m; spreads by seed and by fragments carried by wind and nesting birds; small flowers with spreading petals). Seed germination, strand growth rate, first flowering and festoon age estimated.
